findings.statement: Marketing overspent by $152,200, which is the largest overspend among all departments.
findings.method: SQL JOIN and subtraction to calculate overspend for each department, then ORDER BY overspend DESC
findings.code: SELECT b.department, b.budget, a.actual, (a.actual - b.budget) AS overspend FROM budget_2025_budget b JOIN budget_2025_actual a ON b.department = a.department ORDER BY overspend DESC

data_quality_notes: No null values in either table (budget_2025_budget and budget_2025_actual)
No duplicate rows in either table
All columns have integer types with no type problems
Both tables contain exactly 8 rows each, representing 8 departments
assumptions: Budget and actual spending are measured in the same currency unit (dollars)
The budget_2025_budget table represents planned spending for 2025
The budget_2025_actual table represents actual spending incurred by the end of 2025
limitations: Only 8 departments are included in the dataset, limiting generalizability to larger organizations
No temporal breakdown available - overspend is calculated as a single aggregate for each department
Cannot determine if overspending was due to one-time events or systemic issues without additional data
